Stock generated bodies are unmodified. The compiled file adds exactly the recorded ten scoped provider binders; reversing them recovers the exact stock bytes. Their implicit parameters are authored Lean-signature adaptations, audited separately from LLBC normalization.

Generated fixed-observation proofs and audited runtime contexts use the fresh optional-slot poll. Runtime contexts retain the generated call structure and admit independently returning Bool/U64 reads and reservations. Projection and refusal laws establish the recorded finite public-call contracts under the explicit library and handle mapping.

Owner checks use identity and immutable-heap contracts. Allocation and reservation use explicit supplied operations with no success assumption; returning reservation refusal is distinct from backend failure. Required value, owner, sequence or capacity contracts belong to the consuming theorem.

The providers are pure per-invocation interpretations, not evolving allocator histories. The active Vec model has no capacity field. Allocator, destructor and reference-count implementations remain trusted. Per-call constructor contracts and the returning-event public checker compose without assuming a deterministic allocator across calls.

The public oracle::check and owned checked::check_interpretation wrappers are selected directly. Owned acceptance/accessor/move operations retain their actual bodies; derived Clone and Debug are not selected. Generated-call proof scope is recorded separately in verification.json. Selection and dependency binding alone do not establish runtime correspondence; the separately source-checked contexts and kernel runtime proofs provide the recorded finite-call correspondence.
Source inventory and artifact hashes establish provenance, not end-to-end solver correctness.

Returning-event keys preserve local cancellation, slot and deadline owner/field identity. The optional slot read uses the actual U64 comparison with the captured active word. The ghost-clear representative changes only unused fixed observations. Responses are overapproximated; physical addresses, atomic memory-model implementations, CAS lifecycle, generation allocation/retirement and scheduler/timer behavior remain outside this package.

The atomic-choice model additions are concrete pure definitions for two trusted library contracts. Option.or_else preserves fallback failure/divergence and does not invoke it for Some. Generic signatures do not establish arbitrary Rust drop effects; the selected inputs are scalar indices and shared theory data.
